terms.comment: From lēvis, smooth; classical in the sense “smooth”. No source gives an ironing board.
Morgan–Owens: an iron is simply ferrum.

evidence: Mart. 2.46.3: tua collūcent prēla lacernīs (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: made of iron, iron; hard, unfeeling
evidence: Caes. BG 5.12.4: Britannī ūtuntur aut aere aut tāleīs ferreīs … prō nummō (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Britannī ūtuntur aut aere aut tāleīs ferreīs … prō nummō
phrases.english: the Britons use either bronze or iron bars for money

phrases.latin: Subūculam tibi lēvigābō, dum tū lūdis.
phrases.english: I’ll iron your shirt while you play.

phrases.latin: Cavē: ferrum calidum est. Lēvigāre est meum, nōn tuum.
phrases.english: Careful: the iron is hot. Ironing is my job, not yours.

sources: Lewis & Short: premo · Lewis & Short: levigo · Lewis & Short: prelum · Lewis & Short: subucula
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. laundry (place to wash clothes), laundry: do the laundry, iron (clothes), soap: laundry detergent, laundry: dry cleaner’s.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 38, 123, 124, 303, 307, 317, 334, 338, 404.
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 64, s.v. stirare.
